seo.title: Google Business Profile Booking Button Guide
seo.meta_description: How to add a booking button to your Google Business Profile through Reserve with Google providers, costs, timing and waitlists, for OC businesses.

h1: Google Business Profile Booking Button: Set Up Bookings on Google
answer: A Google Business Profile booking button lets customers book directly from your profile through a supported booking provider, using Reserve with Google. Google says your provider may charge you, providers appear on your profile within a week, and you can use your own link instead. Anaheim and Orange County salons, studios, clinics and restaurants can turn searches into appointments.
key_takeaways: You can use your own link instead.

sections.heading: How booking through Google works
sections.body_html: Google's help page says that when you manage bookings through a booking provider, customers get services that work with their Google accounts, reminders for appointments and easy use of products like Calendar. Reserve with Google is the program that connects supported providers.

sections.heading: Check costs first
sections.body_html: Google says that when you book through Google, your provider might charge you, and to check with your provider for details. Compare that cost with taking bookings through your own link.

sections.heading: Turn on bookings
sections.body_html: Go to your Business Profile and select Bookings. To sign up your preferred provider, select Get started, choose your provider and select Done. Google says booking providers appear on your profile within a week.

sections.heading: No provider yet?
sections.body_html: If you do not work with a provider, Google says you can find providers available in your country through Reserve with Google, or add your own booking link to your profile.

sections.heading: Custom links versus providers
sections.body_html: Google notes that performance data is not available for custom links. With a provider, you can check booking performance through Reserve with Google. Weigh the reporting against any provider fees.

sections.heading: Waitlists for restaurants
sections.body_html: Google says waitlists are available only for restaurants, through an eligible third-party Reserve with Google provider. You can add providers, manage waitlists and view performance from your profile; to remove the Join waitlist button, you unregister with the provider.

sections.heading: Businesses that benefit most
sections.body_html:
• Salons, barbershops and spas.
  • Fitness and yoga studios.
  • Clinics and wellness practices.
  • Restaurants taking reservations or waitlists.

sections.heading: Keep availability accurate
sections.body_html: Bookings only work if your provider's calendar matches reality. Keep staff schedules, services and prices current, especially before holidays.

sections.heading: Bookings and reviews
sections.body_html: Customers who book through Google are good candidates for review requests afterwards. Ask every customer, not just those who book online.

sections.heading: Bookings and AI assistants
sections.body_html: As AI assistants start booking on people's behalf, being bookable through standard systems makes your business easier to choose.

sections.heading: Checklist
sections.body_html:
• Provider chosen and fees checked.
  • Bookings turned on from the profile.
  • Or your own booking link added.
  • Availability and services accurate.
  • Waitlist set up if you're a restaurant.
  • Review requests sent after appointments.

sections.heading: Common booking setup mistakes
sections.body_html:
• Turning on a provider without checking its fees for bookings made through Google.
  • Letting the provider's calendar fall out of step with real staff schedules.
  • Offering services online that need a consultation first, which leads to cancellations.
  • Forgetting to update availability before holidays and closures.
  • Expecting performance data for a custom link, which Google says is not available.

sections.heading: Is a booking button right for you?
sections.body_html: A booking button suits businesses where customers book a set service for a set time: haircuts, nails, massages, fitness classes, restaurant tables and many health appointments. It suits jobs that need a quote or site visit less well; those businesses are usually better served by a clear quote request link. Before you turn bookings on, check how you take bookings today, how much each one costs you through each route, and whether your team can keep the online calendar accurate. For salons, studios and restaurants in Anaheim and across Orange County, a working booking button can capture customers who decide late in the evening, long after the phones are off.

sections.heading: An example
sections.body_html: Imagine a hair salon in Huntington Beach that already uses a booking system supported by Reserve with Google. The owner checks the provider's fees, selects Bookings, then Get started, and chooses the provider. Within a week, a booking button appears on the profile. The salon keeps stylists' schedules up to date and sends review requests after appointments.

sections.heading: How this fits your local plan
sections.body_html: Treat this as part of a routine rather than a one-off fix. Local visibility in Anaheim and the rest of Orange County comes from many small, accurate signals adding up: a verified profile, consistent listings, useful service pages, real photos and a flow of honest reviews. Google is open that relevance, distance and popularity drive local results. You cannot change distance, but you can make sure Google and AI assistants understand exactly what you do and see evidence that customers value it. Put a monthly reminder in the calendar to check the profile, read new reviews and update anything that has changed.

sections.heading: Questions owners ask us
sections.body_html: Owners often ask whether a booking button replaces phone bookings. It does not need to: many customers still call, and a button simply adds another route for people who prefer to book online. Another common question is how to change providers. Set up the new provider, then follow the old provider's process to stop bookings through Google, and check the profile afterwards. Owners also ask whether restaurants need both reservations and a waitlist. It depends on how you seat guests; walk-in-heavy restaurants may benefit most from a waitlist, while bookable dining rooms suit reservations. Owners also ask what to do when a customer books a slot that is no longer free. That is a sign the provider calendar and the real schedule are out of step; fix the sync first, then contact the customer quickly with an alternative time. A good habit is to check the online calendar each morning and block out staff holidays, training days and closures well in advance, so that customers who book through Google only ever see times you can actually honor.

sections.heading: What to do this week
sections.body_html:
1. Check if your booking system is a supported provider.
  2. Compare fees with using your own link.
  3. Turn on bookings.
  4. Keep availability current.

sections.heading: When to get help
sections.body_html: You do not need an agency for every step here; Google documents most of it clearly. Consider outside help when the work is urgent and unfamiliar, when you manage several locations, or when the same issue returns after you fix it. Ask any provider to show you the specific guideline or documentation behind each recommendation, to keep you as the owner of your accounts and to report results in calls, bookings and leads rather than vanity numbers. That is how Chimera works with Orange County businesses from our base in Anaheim.

sections.heading: The short version
sections.body_html: Pick a provider, check its fees, turn on bookings from your profile, or add your own link, and keep availability accurate. Chimera, based in Anaheim, helps Orange County businesses choose the right setup.

faqs.q: How do I add a Book button to Google?
faqs.a: Select Bookings on your profile, then Get started and choose a supported provider.

faqs.q: Does booking through Google cost money?
faqs.a: Google says your provider might charge you; check with them.

faqs.q: How long does it take to appear?
faqs.a: Google says booking providers appear on your profile within a week.

faqs.q: Can I use my own booking link?
faqs.a: Yes. You can add your own link instead of a provider.

faqs.q: Are waitlists available for all businesses?
faqs.a: No. Google says waitlists are only for restaurants.
Through Reserve with Google for providers; not for custom links.

faqs.q: Do you help businesses in Anaheim and Orange County with this?
faqs.a: Yes. Chimera is based in Anaheim, California and works with businesses across Orange County, California.
